Where uploaded data is stored
-----------------------------

Before you save uploaded files, the data needs to be stored somewhere.

By default, if an uploaded file is smaller than 2.5 megabytes, Django will hold
the entire contents of the upload in memory. This means that saving the file
involves only a read from memory and a write to disk and thus is very fast.

However, if an uploaded file is too large, Django will write the uploaded file
to a temporary file stored in your system's temporary directory. On a Unix-like
platform this means you can expect Django to generate a file called something
like ``/tmp/tmpzfp6I6.upload``. If an upload is large enough, you can watch this
file grow in size as Django streams the data onto disk.

These specifics -- 2.5 megabytes; ``/tmp``; etc. -- are simply "reasonable
defaults" which can be customized as described in the next section.

``FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS``
---------------------------

Default: ``None``

The numeric mode (i.e. ``0o644``) to set newly uploaded files to. For more
information about what these modes mean, see the documentation for `os.chmod`_.

If ``None``, files will be saved with the permissions that the operating system
gives new files. On most platforms, this means the file will have the
permissions that the process was started with, which may be affected by the
``umask``.

Where uploaded data is stored
-----------------------------

Before you save uploaded files, the data needs to be stored somewhere.

By default, if an uploaded file is smaller than 2.5 megabytes, Django will hold
the entire contents of the upload in memory. This means that saving the file
involves only a read from memory and a write to disk and thus is very fast.

However, if an uploaded file is too large, Django will write the uploaded file
to a temporary file stored in your system's temporary directory. On a Unix-like
platform this means you can expect Django to generate a file called something
like ``/tmp/tmpzfp6I6.upload``. If an upload is large enough, you can watch this
file grow in size as Django streams the data onto disk.

These specifics -- 2.5 megabytes; ``/tmp``; etc. -- are simply "reasonable
defaults" which can be customized as described in the next section.

Where uploaded data is stored
-----------------------------

Before you save uploaded files, the data needs to be stored somewhere.

By default, if an uploaded file is smaller than 2.5 megabytes, Django will hold
the entire contents of the upload in memory. This means that saving the file
involves only a read from memory and a write to disk and thus is very fast.

However, if an uploaded file is too large, Django will write the uploaded file
to a temporary file stored in your system's temporary directory. On a Unix-like
platform this means you can expect Django to generate a file called something
like ``/tmp/tmpzfp6I6.upload``. If an upload is large enough, you can watch this
file grow in size as Django streams the data onto disk.

These specifics -- 2.5 megabytes; ``/tmp``; etc. -- are simply "reasonable
defaults" which can be customized as described in the next section.

.. warning::

    When saving files to a :class:`~django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage`,
    the permissions of the resulting file may differ depending on whether the
    uploaded file was stored in memory or on disk as a temporary file. This is
    because temporary files created by Python's ``tempfile`` module are created
    with restrictive permissions (``0o600``) for security reasons. If you need
    consistent file permissions, set the :setting:`FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS`
    setting explicitly.

    def test_file_save_without_name(self):
        """
        File storage extracts the filename from the content object if no
        name is given explicitly.
        """
        self.assertFalse(self.storage.exists('test.file'))

        f.name = 'test.file'

        storage_f_name = self.storage.save(None, f)

        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.temp_dir, f.name)))

        self.storage.delete(storage_f_name)

    def test_file_permissions_default(self):
        """
        File storage uses the default file permissions (0o644) when
        FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS is not set.
        """
        self.assertFalse(self.storage.exists('test.file'))

        f = ContentFile('custom contents')
        f_name = self.storage.save('test.file', f)
        self.addCleanup(self.storage.delete, f_name)

        mode = os.stat(self.storage.path(f_name)).st_mode & 0o777
        self.assertEqual(mode, 0o644)
